A single drop hangs from the very tip of one leaf, round and still, with the whole grey mist curved and reversed inside it.
A moss curtain covers an entire vertical face of bark, water running steadily down the whole sheet, lit from behind so the moving water reads white.
One orchid flowers out of a crack in the bark so narrow the crack itself is invisible, nothing else growing anywhere near it.
The same orchid at three sizes at once: one wide wet flower close in the frame, a spray of them halfway back, and specks of the same colour lost in the mist.
Standing water in the cupped centre of a stiff ring of strappy leaves, so still it holds a perfect reversed picture of the branches above.
A line of drops along the whole underside of one limb, each hanging at exactly the same length, perfectly spaced.
One flower still bent in the shape of the leaf that lay across it until this morning, the crease not yet straightened out.
Pale flat roots spreading right across bare bark, clamped hard to the wood, bare bark showing in the gaps between them.
A strip of bark peeled and curled away from the trunk and caught a whole pool of water inside the curl.
A spent flower lying face-up on the moss below the plant that dropped it, still holding its full colour.
One dead limb carrying more growing things than any living limb in the frame, every centimetre of it packed.
A small stream running along the top of one limb in its own shallow worn channel, with plants drinking from it the whole length.
A fern frond so thin that the full outline of the leaf behind it shows straight through it.
A hanging moss strand grown so long it has reached the limb below and begun attaching there, still connected to the strand above.
One flowering plant whose every bloom has turned to face the single gap in the mist cover above.
A ring of paler moss on the bark where something sat for a long time and has only recently gone.
Water beading on a waxy leaf in dozens of separate spheres, each one a different size, none of them running.
A thick pad of moss on the upper side of a limb so saturated it is visibly sagging away from the bark under its own weight.
A root that has grown down off its branch, hung free in the air for a stretch, then found the bark of the limb below and gripped it.
One broad flat flower pressed so close to its bark that the texture of the bark shows through the base of the petals.
Water dripping from one point on an overhang in a single thin continuous thread, the thread catching the diffuse light and reading silver.
A cluster of small flowers on the shaded underside of a branch, turned downward and outward, every one facing away from the bark.
A length of bark completely hidden under overlapping layers of flat grey-green leaves laid one on the next like wet paper.
Mist condensing on a vertical root and running down it in a steady visible trickle, the root darker at the base from constant wet.
Two branches crossing close together, the narrow angle between them filled completely with moss and standing water, the water level perfectly flat.
